exercises.title: Fix a broken YAML file (the lab of Chapter 5)
exercises.task: This file has three mistakes. Fix them one by one: read the message, go to the line and column it gives, fix, check again. At the end, config must be a mapping with the key schema.
exercises.start:
version: 2

models:
  - name: stg_payments
    description: Payments from Stripe: one row per payment
    columns:
      - name: payment_id
        data_tests:
          - unique
          - not_null
     - name: amount_usd
        description: "Amount in dollars"
      - name: status
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: [success, fail]
    config:
      schema:{{ target.schema }}
exercises.solution:
version: 2

models:
  - name: stg_payments
    description: "Payments from Stripe: one row per payment"
    columns:
      - name: payment_id
        data_tests:
          - unique
          - not_null
      - name: amount_usd
        description: "Amount in dollars"
      - name: status
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: [success, fail]
    config:
      schema: "{{ target.schema }}"

values.equals: Payments from Stripe: one row per payment
values.label: the description

exercises.hint: First error: a colon followed by a space inside the description. Put the whole description in double quotes.
exercises.why: YAML reads "key: value" pairs. A second ": " in a value, a list item one space out of line, or a missing space after a colon change what YAML sees.

exercises.title: A tab instead of spaces
exercises.task: Line 5 starts with a TAB character. YAML allows only spaces for indentation. Replace the tab by 4 spaces.
exercises.hint: Delete the invisible character at the start of line 5, then type 4 spaces.
exercises.why: A tab looks like spaces in many editors, but YAML refuses it: "found a tab character that violates indentation".

exercises.title: A missing space after the colon
exercises.task: dbt says "mapping values are not allowed in this context" on line 5. The real mistake is on line 4. Find it and fix it.
exercises.hint: Without a space, "name:stg_orders" is one text, not a key and a value.
exercises.why: YAML needs a space after the colon of a key. The error is reported where YAML gets lost (line 5), not where the mistake is.

exercises.title: Quote the Jinja
exercises.task: A value that starts with {{ must be in quotes, otherwise YAML reads { as the start of a mapping. Fix the schema line.
exercises.start:
version: 2

models:
  - name: stg_orders
    config:
      schema: {{ target.schema }}
exercises.solution:
version: 2

models:
  - name: stg_orders
    config:
      schema: "{{ target.schema }}"
exercises.why: In YAML, { starts an inline mapping. dbt renders the Jinja later, but first the file must be valid YAML.

exercises.title: A typo in a key (bug 9 of Chapter 22)
exercises.task: This file is valid YAML and dbt on DuckDB says nothing, but one description is lost. Find the key with a typo and fix it.
exercises.start:
version: 2

models:
  - name: fct_orders
    description: One row per order, with the amount paid (successful payments only).
    config:
      group: finance
      access: public
      event_time: order_date
      tags: ['finance']
      meta:
        owner: finance-team
        contains_pii: false
    columns:
      - name: order_id
        description: Primary key of the order.
        data_tests:
          - unique
          - not_null
      - name: status
        description: "{{ doc('order_status') }}"
      - name: amount
        description: Total of the successful payments, in dollars (0 when not paid yet).
        data_tests:
          - is_positive:
              arguments:
                allow_zero: true

  - name: fct_monthly_revenue
    desciption: Orders and revenue per order month and customer country (returned orders excluded).
    config:
      group: finance
      access: public
      tags: ['finance']
    data_tests:
      - dbt_utils.unique_combination_of_columns:
          arguments:
            combination_of_columns: ['order_month', 'country']

  - name: fct_order_items
    description: One row per order line (order x product), with the line amount in dollars.
    config:
      group: finance
      access: protected
      event_time: order_date
      tags: ['finance']
    data_tests:
      - dbt_utils.unique_combination_of_columns:
          arguments:
            combination_of_columns: ['order_id', 'product_id']
      - dbt_utils.expression_is_true:
          arguments:
            expression: "line_amount = quantity * unit_price"
    columns:
      - name: order_item_key
        description: Surrogate key (hash of order_id and product_id).
        data_tests:
          - unique
          - not_null
      - name: quantity
        data_tests:
          - dbt_utils.accepted_range:
              arguments:
                min_value: 1
                max_value: 10

  - name: fct_order_items_daily
    description: Quantity and revenue per day and product (microbatch incremental model).
    config:
      group: finance
      access: protected
      tags: ['finance']

  - name: customer_segments
    description: One row per customer with a marketing segment and a value tier (Python model, pandas).
    config:
      group: marketing
      access: protected
      tags: ['marketing']
    columns:
      - name: customer_id
        description: Primary key.
        data_tests:
          - unique
          - not_null
      - name: segment
        description: no orders, new, regular or loyal.

exercises.title: columns must be a list
exercises.task: This is valid YAML, but dbt refuses it: columns is a mapping here, dbt wants a list of columns, each with a name. Rewrite it as a list.
exercises.start:
version: 2

models:
  - name: stg_stripe__payments
    columns:
      payment_id:
        description: Primary key.
exercises.solution:
version: 2

models:
  - name: stg_stripe__payments
    columns:
      - name: payment_id
        description: Primary key.
exercises.why: dbt validates the shape of properties files: "at path ['columns'] ... is not of type 'array'".

exercises.title: A zip code that becomes a number
exercises.task: Python reads zip: 01234 as the number 668 (an old octal rule). Make it read the text 01234.
exercises.why: YAML guesses types: numbers, booleans and dates are converted unless you quote them.
